title: Metastability
description: The double well $\Psi = \frac{(x^2 - 4)^2}{16} + \frac{y^2}{2}$ has its minima at $x = \pm 2$ and a saddle at the origin, a barrier of height $\Delta\Psi = 1$. All particles start in the left well. The First passage window measures $\tau = \inf\{t : X^1_t > 0\}$, the time to reach the saddle. Kramers' law says $\mathbb{E}\tau \propto e^{2\Delta\Psi/\sigma^2}$ for small σ.

questions.text: Press play and wait until all particles have arrived. What is $\mathbb{E}\tau$ at σ = 1? (The check compares with what the app measured.)
Kramers' law: by what factor should $\mathbb{E}\tau$ grow when σ goes from 1 to 0.8?
Set σ = 0.8, restart the measurement (button in the window) with all particles back in the left well, and measure again. Does the factor match Kramers' law? What could explain a difference?
Is $\tau$ roughly exponentially distributed? Look at the shape of $P(\tau \le t)$.
